Shaker Heights' Tree Protection Ordinance & City Tree Commission

Shaker Heights maintains a tree protection ordinance and an active City Tree Commission that reviews work along the public right-of-way and heritage-tree protection above specified DBH (diameter at breast height) thresholds. Roubic assesses DBH before quoting and coordinates the permit workflow on your behalf — we know the city contacts, application forms, and review timelines.

Dead or dying hazard trees follow an expedited process with arborist documentation. When a permit fee applies, it passes through at the city's actual cost — disclosed upfront in the quote, with no markup and no surprise charges.

What Happens If You Defer

The Cost of Waiting — Shaker Heights Context

Three scenarios that turn a $700 removal into a $3,000 emergency job.

EAB Ash Stability Degradation

Emerald Ash Borer has killed an estimated 90%+ of NE Ohio's ash. EAB-killed ash turn brittle within 18–24 months and fail violently in storms — many standing dead ash across Shaker Heights are now the fragile ones.

Wind-Load Failures

Shaker Heights' mature heritage canopy takes hard wind hits every spring. Leaning or dead-crown trees near homes and garages become insurance-deductible events once they fail.

Right-of-Way & Ordinance Exposure

Hazard trees threatening the public right-of-way fall under City Tree Commission review. Left unremediated after notice, they can escalate to city action — the removal cost stays the same, but the timeline no longer belongs to you.

Common Shaker Heights Removal Questions

Shaker Heights Tree Removal FAQ

Six things Shaker Heights homeowners want to know before booking.

How much does tree removal cost in Shaker Heights?
Shaker Heights tree removal typically runs $200–$10,000+ depending on size, species, access, and any permit fees. Confirmed brackets: small trees under 30 ft $300–$700; medium 30–60 ft $700–$1,800; large heritage 60–80 ft $1,800–$3,500; X-large 80+ ft requiring crane support $3,500–$7,000+. Emergency and after-hours work adds roughly a 30% premium. Every estimate is free on-site.
Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Shaker Heights?
Shaker Heights maintains a tree protection ordinance and a City Tree Commission that requires a permit for healthy-tree removal above a specified DBH threshold, plus review of work along the public right-of-way. Dead or dying hazard trees follow an expedited process with arborist documentation. Roubic assesses DBH before quoting and coordinates the permit workflow at no separate fee — only the city's actual permit cost passes through, disclosed upfront.
How quickly can Roubic remove a tree in Shaker Heights?
Shaker Heights is a Tier 2 Roubic service area — standard removals typically schedule within a few business days of estimate sign-off, and active emergencies (tree on structure, blocking a driveway, leaning hazard) get next-day or after-hours response from our Auburn Township yard, 14 miles away. Call {{global.phone}} for emergency dispatch on the 24/7 line.
Will Roubic remove an EAB-killed ash tree in Shaker Heights?
Yes. Emerald Ash Borer has killed an estimated 90%+ of ash trees in NE Ohio — including Shaker Heights — and EAB-killed ash become brittle within 18–24 months, failing violently in storms. We've removed hundreds of EAB-killed ash across the area; the wood is hauled to our Auburn Township firewood yard for seasoning.
Does Roubic coordinate with the Shaker Heights City Tree Commission?
Yes — City Tree Commission coordination is routine for us. The commission reviews tree work along public right-of-way and heritage-tree protection above specified DBH thresholds. We know the city contacts, application forms, and review timelines, and we handle that workflow as part of the job so you aren't left navigating it alone.
Can Roubic handle crane-assisted heritage removals in Shaker Heights?
Yes — for very-large heritage trees (80+ ft) or removals over structures where standard rigging isn't feasible, Roubic coordinates crane access on-site. This is common on Shaker Heights' tight-access historic lots along the Shaker Boulevard corridor and in the Lomond neighborhood. Crane-assisted removals start around $3,500; exact scope is confirmed during the free estimate walk.
